summary.en: The Colombian Army conducted an airstrike in Nariño that killed eight ELN members and a separate bombing in the southwest killed eight ELN fighters, while President De la Espriella launched a total offensive against the ELN and dissident FARC in Arauca. A drone attack injured six police officers at a station and a Black Hawk crash left thirteen soldiers stranded in Cauca. An illegal gold mine collapse in southwestern Colombia killed fourteen miners and injured seven. A priest survived a cross falling on him in a church and a gang killed a preacher. The conflict recorded 225 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Den colombianske hæren utførte et luftangrep i Nariño som drepte åtte ELN-medlemmer, og et separat bombangrep i sørvest drepte åtte ELN-krigere, mens president De la Espriella lanserte en total offensiv mot ELN og dissidente FARC i Arauca. Et droneangrep såret seks politifolk på en stasjon, og en Black-Hawk-ulykke etterlot tretten soldater strandet i Cauca. Et ulovlig gullgruvekollaps i sørvestlige Colombia drepte fjorten gruvearbeidere og såret sju. En prest overlevde da et kors falt på ham i en kirke, og en gjeng drepte en predikant. Konflikten registrerte 225 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
